# Results — Study 127 (Williams-R) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Larry Williams' %R(14):
on the daily chart, buy when %R falls below −80 (oversold) and sell/short when it rises
above −20 (overbought). Two framings: (1) **zone entry** — enter on the first bar inside
the extreme zone, hold *N* days; (2) **cross-back** — enter when %R exits the extreme
zone (the "confirmed reversal"). Both tested against a random-direction control on the
same entry bars. As-of **2026-06-14**.*

*Instruments: SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL, TSLA, NVDA. Window: 10 years daily. Total trades
pooled: **n = 2,111** (~35 signals/ticker/year).*

## The honest test — zone entry vs a random-direction control (hold = 5 days, gross)

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **%R zone entry (with the signal)** | 2,111 | **47.7%** | **−9.5** | −0.26 | **−0.88** |
| Random direction (control) | 2,111 | 50.0% | −1.2 | — | −0.12 |

- The zone-entry's gross expectancy is **−9.5 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **−0.88** —
  statistically **indistinguishable from zero** and on the wrong side of it.
- It does **not beat the coin.** Zone − random = **−8.3 bps/trade**.
- Per-instrument, no tape carries a real edge: every HAC |*t*| < 1.5
  (SPY −1.40, QQQ −0.11, IWM −0.12, AAPL −1.46, TSLA −0.82, NVDA +0.89).

## Cross-back framing (confirmed reversal, hold = 5 days, gross)

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **%R cross-back (with the signal)** | 2,111 | **46.1%** | **−24.6** | **−2.14** |
| Random direction (control) | 2,111 | 49.8% | +10.1 | +0.94 |

The cross-back framing is **worse** than the zone entry — it earns −24.6 bps/trade at
HAC *t* = −2.14, which is a statistically significant negative result. Far from
confirming a bounce, the "confirmed reversal" signal tends to enter *after* the move
has already happened.

## Hold-period sweep (zone entry, pooled, gross)

| Hold (days) | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 2,111 | 50.0% | +2.9 | +0.75 |
| 3 | 2,111 | 48.2% | −4.7 | −0.63 |
| 5 | 2,111 | 47.7% | −9.5 | −0.88 |
| 10 | 2,111 | 47.8% | −24.9 | −1.33 |

No horizon clears the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar. The 1-day result is positive but noisy (*t* = +0.75),
suggesting any momentum in the oversold bounce reverses over the following days — consistent
with a market that has already priced the event.

## Cost sweep (zone entry, hold = 5 days)

~35 signals/ticker/year means costs are modest relative to the turnover — but the gross is
already negative, so costs only deepen the hole:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −9.5 | −0.88 |
| 0.5 bps | −10.0 | −0.93 |
| 1.0 bps | −10.5 | −0.97 |
| 2.0 bps | −11.5 | −1.07 |

The gross edge is already negative, so there is **no positive break-even cost**. The
strategy was never alive for costs to kill.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_daily`), the same zone-entry
engine recovers a %R edge **only when mean-reversion is planted**, and reads ≈ 0 when the
tape is a martingale — confirming the rule is a faithful mean-reversion detector, and that
the real tape simply does not carry the structure %R is designed to harvest:

| Planted mean-rev (AR(1) coefficient) | %R gross (bps/trade) | beats random control? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ 0 (coin) | no |
| +0.30 (mean-reverting) | positive | yes |
| −0.15 (trending) | negative | no (wrong side) |

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Zone-entry gross HAC *t* = −0.88 (wrong sign); no evidence of
  any directional information over a random-direction control (Δ = −8.3 bps/trade); no
  instrument clears |*t*| ≥ 1.5. Cross-back framing is actively negative (*t* = −2.14),
  disconfirming the "confirmed reversal" folk recipe.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Gross expectancy already negative at −9.5 bps/trade; no
  positive break-even cost exists. The oversold/overbought signal does not reliably
  predict a bounce on daily equity data over the 2016–2026 window.
